study_identification_part.si4_title: Characterizing the distinct imaging phenotypes, clinical behavior, and genetic vulnerability of brain maturational subtypes in mood disorders

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To quantify brain morphological heterogeneity in mood disorders by mapping regional gray matter volume (GMV) changes at the individual patient level, using normative modeling to identify subtypes within MDD and BD patients, and characterize these subtypes using clinical behaviors, cell-specific transcriptomic profiles, and polygenic risk scores.

nm10_nm_vldtn_diff_domain.reason: The study validated the GMV deviations-based subtyping in an independent replication cohort (Dataset 2) consisting of 268 medicated patients from the same institution. The regional GMV deviation patterns identified in Dataset 1 (drug-naïve/drug-free patients) were validated for reproducibility in Dataset 2. Specifically, the top 10 regions with supra-normal deviations in subtype 1 and infra-normal deviations in subtype 2 were found to be consistent across both datasets, and group-averaged regional GMV deviation values showed significant correlations between datasets (subtype 1: r=0.29, p<0.05; subtype 2: r=0.45, p<0.0001).

caa6_deviation_metric.answer: Z-scores from quantile regression (z5, z50, z95); supra-normal defined as z95 > 1.96 (exceeding 95% CI for 95th percentile); infra-normal defined as z5 < -1.96 (below 5% CI for 5th percentile); categorical encoding: -1 (infra-normal), 0 (normal), +1 (supra-normal); average abnormality rate (percentage of GMV deviation); average abnormality extent (mean z95 or z5 values)
caa6_deviation_metric.reason: The methods section provides detailed description of how deviations were quantified. Three continuous z-scores were calculated (z5, z50, z95) representing deviations from the 5th, 50th, and 95th percentiles. Extreme deviations were defined using bootstrapped confidence intervals: supra-normal as z95 > 1.96 and infra-normal as z5 < -1.96. Patients were then categorically encoded as -1, 0, or +1. Summary metrics included average abnormality rate and extent.
caa6_deviation_metric.supporting_text: We positioned individuals with MDD and BD on the normative percentile charts based on HC and expressed three kinds of continuous measurement of deviation from the generated normative range including the 5th percentile (z5) quantile regression predictor, the 50th percentile (z50) quantile regression predictor and the 95th percentile (z95) quantile regression predictor... We used z scores to quantify individual GMV deviation from the 5% and 95%... We defined the supra-normal as any individual exceeding the 95% CI for the 95th percentile (z95 > 1.96), and infra-normal as any individual below the 5% CI for the 5th percentile (z5 < -1.96). Each patient was represented with a GMV deviation encoding map in which brain areas were numerically encoded with either -1 (infra-normal), 0 (normal), or +1 (supra-normal)

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Hierarchical clustering with Ward's linkage on individual z50 GMV deviation maps to identify subtypes; 10-fold cross-validation with 1000 permutations using adjusted rand index (ARI) for clustering stability; two-sample t-tests comparing clinical measures (HAMD, HAMA, BPRS total scores) between subtypes with FDR correction (pFDR < 0.05); WCST cognitive performance comparisons between subtypes and HC with FDR correction; symptom network analysis using graph theory with Pearson correlations (r >= 0.2 threshold) for HAMD, HAMA, and BPRS items, comparing global network density and strength between subtypes using paired t-tests; partial least squares (PLS) regression for transcriptome-imaging associations (5000 permutations, p < 0.05) with spatial bootstrapping to rank genes; Gene Ontology and KEGG pathway enrichment using Metascape (pFDR < 0.05); virtual histology analysis overlapping PLS genes with cell-type specific gene sets (seven cell types) using permutation tests and chi-squared tests (pFDR < 0.05); polygenic risk score (PRS) analysis using logistic regression for PRS-AD and PRS-MDD at multiple p-value thresholds (1.0e-06 to 0.1) with FDR correction (pFDR < 0.05), reporting Nagelkerke's pseudo-R²; validation of GMV deviation patterns in independent Dataset 2 using Pearson correlations of regional z50 maps between datasets
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Two subtypes were identified: subtype 1 with supra-normal GMV deviations in frontal cortex, cognitive impairment, higher AD genetic risk, and transcriptional associations with AD pathways and oligodendrocytes/endothelial cells; subtype 2 with globally decreased GMV deviations, more severe depressive symptoms, higher MDD genetic vulnerability, and transcriptional associations with microglia and inhibitory neurons.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Hierarchical clustering based on GMV deviations identified two transdiagnostic subtypes across MDD and BD. Subtype 1 (n=112; 74 MDD, 38 BD) showed supra-normal GMV deviations particularly in frontal cortex (orbitofrontal, rostral middle frontal), cingulate cortex, and paracentral cortex (z95 > 1.96), with >57% of brain regions showing supra-normal patterns. This subtype demonstrated significantly impaired executive function on WCST (PE: t=4.00, pFDR=0.001; CR: t=-3.65, pFDR=0.001; CC: t=-3.63, pFDR=0.001; TE: t=3.61, pFDR=0.001) compared to HC. PRS analysis revealed significantly higher AD genetic risk at four p-value thresholds (explaining 4.2-5.9% variance, pFDR<0.05). PLS transcriptomic analysis (explaining 26.38% covariance, r=0.52, p=0.0017) showed enrichment in AD pathways, cell/blood morphogenesis, and cellular component pathways, with significant association to endothelial cells and oligodendrocytes. Subtype 2 (n=62; 40 MDD, 22 BD) exhibited widespread infra-normal GMV deviations across frontal, temporal, parietal, and cingulate cortices (z5 < -1.96) in 90% of cortical regions, with supra-normal deviation only in occipital cortex. This subtype had significantly higher HAMD total scores than subtype 1 (t=2.67, pFDR=0.025), with more prominent guilt, early insomnia, insight, and somatic symptoms. Symptom network analysis revealed higher global network density (0.51 vs 0.42) and strength (6.76 vs 5.24) in subtype 2 compared to subtype 1 (t=10.17, p=1.0e-06). PRS-MDD at threshold 1.0e-03 showed significant association (explaining 10.8% variance, pFDR<0.05). PLS analysis (explaining variance, r=0.48, p=0.0039) showed enrichment in ion transport, calcium signaling, trans-synaptic signaling, and stress response pathways, with significant enrichment in microglia-related genes (117 overlapped genes, permutation pFDR=0.005) and marginal enrichment in inhibitory neuron genes (157 genes, pFDR=0.057). Regional GMV deviation patterns were validated in an independent dataset of 268 medicated patients (Dataset 2), with significant correlations between datasets for both subtypes (subtype 1: r=0.29, p<0.05; subtype 2: r=0.45, p<0.0001), and the top 10 regions showing consistent deviation patterns across datasets.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Use of healthy brain gene expression data from AHBA to explain patient GMV deviations may not reflect actual patient transcription; AHBA right hemisphere data limited to two participants, restricting spatial correlation analysis; small genetic data sample size; cognitive assessment limited to WCST only; lack of illness severity data for first episode in medication-free patients; unable to detect associations between GMV alterations and prior depressive/anxious/psychotic symptoms
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: First, the use of gene expression profiles from the healthy human brain in AHBA to explain GMV deviations changes is limited to the extent that transcription in patients could be different from those in healthy brains. Additionally, the AHBA gene expression data including the right hemisphere of the brain for only two participants, restricts the representation of the spatial correlation between entire brain transcriptional level and GMV deviations... Second, the genetic data size in our study was small... Third, we only used WSCT scores to test cognitive functions between subtype groups. Some other cognitive batteries would be validated in future work. Fourth, we did not obtain specific data about illness severity of the first episode in medication-free patients and were not able to detect the associations between GMV alterations and prior depressive/anxious/psychotic symptoms.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: The study used a trans-diagnostic approach, identifying subtypes across traditional MDD/BD diagnostic boundaries, with both disorders represented in each subtype. A replication cohort of medicated patients (Dataset 2) was used to validate imaging phenotypes, demonstrating reproducibility of GMV deviation patterns. Symptom networks were constructed using HAMD, HAMA, and BPRS items (including 5-factor BPRS solution) to compare network topology between subtypes. The integration of multi-omics data (neuroimaging, transcriptomics via AHBA, and genomics via PRS) provided multidimensional characterization of biological heterogeneity. Only drug-naïve or drug-free (>2 months) patients were included in the discovery cohort to minimize medication confounders.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This study applied normative modeling using quantile regression to identify individual-level GMV deviations in mood disorders, then used unsupervised hierarchical clustering to identify two biologically distinct subtypes. The approach differs from traditional case-control designs by focusing on inter-individual variability. The study is notable for integrating neuroimaging-based subtyping with spatial transcriptomics (AHBA), polygenic risk scores, clinical phenotyping, and cognitive assessments to provide comprehensive characterization of heterogeneity. The two identified subtypes showed opposite brain developmental patterns (supra-normal vs infra-normal dominant) with distinct genetic vulnerabilities (AD risk vs MDD risk), cell-type associations (oligodendrocytes/endothelial cells vs microglia/inhibitory neurons), and clinical presentations (cognitive impairment vs severe depressive symptoms). Left hemisphere only analysis was conducted due to limited AHBA right hemisphere data (only 2 donors). The study included both a discovery cohort (174 drug-naïve/drug-free patients) and a replication cohort (268 medicated patients) from the same institution. Clustering stability was rigorously assessed using 10-fold cross-validation with 1000 permutations and ARI scores.
